subject: Platform auth anomaly notification + SIG evidence request
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@finserv.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Suspicious auth pattern on FinServCo org - need IRP + SIG extracts

Hi Marissa,

Quick heads-up from our side: our monitoring picked up an unusual spike of failed and then successful token exchanges against service accounts tied to our FinServCo tenant that call your hosted API. The pattern suggests credential reuse across multiple IP ranges, followed by a handful of calls that included sensitive account-scoped endpoints.

We need two things from Redwood immediately:
- A brief notification of whether this is a platform-level issue or an isolated customer/credential compromise.
- A packaged set of technical artifacts we can present to our internal security team and auditors: session logs, auth header traces (redacted where required), and a SIG/SOC2 evidence export that maps logging controls to your SOC 2 control IDs.

If you can confirm receipt and an ETA for the artifacts, that would help our incident timeline. We’re treating this as a potential credential compromise and currently have a high-priority ticket open (JIRA-INC-8792).

Thanks,
Elaine Park
Security Operations, FinServCo

Attachment: sample_alert_screenshot.png (image)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Elaine — thanks for the alert and context. I’ve opened this thread in our inbox and looped in Security (Markus) and Compliance (Stephanie).

Immediate actions from Redwood:
- We’ve isolated the FinServCo API keys in our logs and started a targeted export of auth/session activity for the indicated 72-hour window.
- Markus will lead the IRP triage and coordinate a deeper forensic pull if needed.
- Stephanie will prepare a SIG export and a SOC 2 control mapping document for your auditors.

ETA: we’ll get an initial packet (redacted logs + timeline) to you within 24 hours and the full SIG extract within 48–72 hours. If your team needs a faster turnaround, tell us the required subset and we’ll prioritize.

Next step: Markus will reply with the forensic scope & evidence delivery mechanism.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Suspicious auth pattern on FinServCo org - need IRP + SIG extracts

Hi all — I took a first pass on scope. Summary of our plan:

1) Containment & scope
- Confirmed the calls came from two distinct IP clusters (see brief below). We have temporarily disabled the implicated service key and will keep it disabled until we validate the token lifecycle.
- Scoping window: 2027-09-11T00:00:00Z through 2027-09-14T07:45:00Z (UTC) as a conservative capture.

2) Evidence to collect and how we’ll hand it off
- Auth/session logs (full, with PII redacted) packaged as auth-session-logs-20270914.zip (CSV + index).
- A machine-readable SIG export (control mapping) exported as PDF and CSV: redwood_SIG_export_20270914.pdf (summary) + raw CSV in the Drive folder.
- Request from us: please provide the minimal list of log fields you require for your audit so we don’t overshare anything unnecessary.

3) Chain of custody / transfer
- We will upload artifacts to the shared Drive folder (link below) and grant FinServCo ops temporary access. For higher-sensitivity items we’ll use a signed S3 presigned link delivered to your secops-consultant address.

4) Ask for your team
- Please confirm whether your incident classification requires encrypted evidence transfer or if the Drive share is acceptable.
- Provide any additional artifacts you need (e.g., request IDs, sample requests).

I’m attaching a small proof-of-concept extract (first 1k rows) so your team can validate fields. If you want to engage our forensics partner for deeper memory or host-level capture, we can escalate — that will require a formal engagement.

Markus Klein
Director, Security Engineering — Redwood Inference
Office: +1 (650) 555-0127

Attachments: auth-session-logs-sample.csv (partial extract)
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-redwood-incident-evidence
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@finserv.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Forensics Consulting <secops-consultant@forensics.example.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious auth pattern on FinServCo org - need IRP + SIG extracts

Elaine — following up with the evidence handoff and a brief take on root cause and mitigation: 

What we delivered (links and attachments):
- Uploaded: auth-session-logs-20270914.zip — contains session-level CSVs, token exchange traces (redacted), and IP clusters.
- Uploaded: redwood_SIG_export_20270914.pdf — a SIG mapping that highlights relevant SOC 2 controls (CC6, CC7) and where corresponding logs live.
- Drive folder link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-redwood-incident-evidence (access granted to FinServCo ops).
- JIRA: JIRA-INC-8792 (your ticket).

Preliminary findings:
- Root cause: evidence points to a compromised API key that was used from multiple geographic IPs after being exfiltrated from a developer workstation outside FinServCo’s perimeter. No platform-wide credential store was implicated.
- Impact: limited to the FinServCo tenant. We identified and rotated the compromised key, and we’ve added a short-term rule to block the observed IP clusters for the tenant.

Next steps we recommend (for FinServCo):
- Rotate all service keys tied to developer machines and enable short-lived tokens (we can help with rollout).
- Review workspace access for third-party dev tools; we can share our suggested workspace ACL template.
- If you need a formal postmortem document for your audit, Stephanie will draft an executive summary + technical appendix by EOD tomorrow.

Stephanie: please attach the SOC 2 crosswalk & the proposed exec summary when ready.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_SIG_export_20270914.pdf (summary), auth-session-logs-20270914.zip (full logs)
